Root operating contract, Enterprise Suite spec, task ledger, multispectrum evidence, and audit-chain conventions are preserved.
New control-plane contract crate is under crates/ and cloud-readiness composes it through a workspace path dependency.
The image provenance contract imports and validates the FD-001 tenant-workload manifest and tenant-admission policy before exposing review-only supply-chain guardrails to cloud-readiness.

No external dependency is introduced; the new contract crate depends only on tenant-workload-manifest and tenant-admission-policy workspace crates, and cloud-readiness adds one workspace path dependency.
Enterprise Suite JSON, catalog row, data_class annotations, and multispectrum evidence keep machine-readable shapes.

Validation is deterministic and bounded: manifest validation, admission-policy validation, required controls, all-manifest-workload scope, official doc URL allowlist, source refs, control-kind coverage, workload coverage, duplicate detection, and runtime overclaim flags are checked.
The slice is a small additive contract crate plus readiness composition, avoiding live registry/admission/runtime plumbing until the supply-chain contract is explicit and reviewable.

The gate strengthens the Oyatie Cloud substrate proof by requiring signed provenance, SBOM, vulnerability gate, and admission evidence across all FD-001 manifest workloads before runtime deployment claims.
Negative tests reject missing requirements, duplicate requirements, doc drift, policy-ref drift, missing required controls, missing all-workload scope, and runtime overclaims.
The public API exposes a single contract builder, validator, doc URL extractor, control enum, and explicit nonclaim booleans for readiness reporting.
Focused unit tests and cloud-readiness tests passed; clippy, fmt, catalog, architecture, data-class, and quality-marker scans are included in closeout.

A live registry, Sigstore, scanner, or admission controller integration was deferred because it would require environment-backed evidence; a review-only contract is the smallest honest supply-chain readiness increment.
The contract composes after tenant-workload and tenant-admission contracts and before runtime tenant evidence slices, preserving the staged Oyatie Cloud substrate architecture.

The contract requires OCI digest pinning, Cosign keyless OIDC signature evidence, transparency-log evidence, in-toto/SLSA provenance, builder/source pins, SBOM requirements, vulnerability gate evidence, and false runtime attachment flags.
The slice does not add runtime hot-path execution; later registry/admission work gets bounded validation expectations without creating current runtime load.
Five image-provenance-contract tests and twenty-six cloud-readiness tests cover positive, negative, and nonclaim paths.

FD-001 remains the product goal; Oyatie Cloud is only the substrate proof. The contract cites official OCI, Sigstore, SLSA, in-toto, SPDX, and CycloneDX sources while keeping runtime verification/workload/audit claims blocked until evidence exists.
Enterprise Suite spec, tasks ledger, catalog row, evidence file, and audit chain were updated for CS-ENT-SUITE-IMAGE-PROVENANCE-CONTRACT-001.
The change is additive; reverting the new crate, dependency, readiness fields/tests, spec/task/evidence/audit rows removes the slice without changing existing runtime behavior.

Readiness output now surfaces image provenance contract readiness, requirement count, all-workload scope, SLSA/SBOM/Cosign/admission attachment booleans, and explicit false runtime verification flags.
No reserved facet exception is required for this review-only contract.

Future live substrate work can migrate from the review-only contract by supplying registry, image publication, signature verification, provenance verification, SBOM, scanner, admission runtime, workload, and audit-chain evidence without changing FD-001/Oyatie Cloud claim boundaries.
